deliberation: The remedy is proportionate and directly implements minimum-human-action policy. Repeated routine requests to jimsteeg consume recovery capacity without adding an authorized decision and contradict GI-STEWARD-0002. Replaying unrelated expensive suites after every merge similarly spends runner time without improving evidence for that change. Retaining required checks, relevant post-merge suites, recovery dispatch, and exact-SHA readback preserves accountable integration while reducing volunteer and compute burden. Council Steward advice does not supply Human Steward authorization.
discharged_obligations: Assessed human burden, runner cost, proportionality, maintainability, reversibility, and institutional purpose.
Compared unconditional replay with relevant-suite execution and lightweight readback.
Distinguished routine authorization, optional review, recovery ownership, and Council advice.
findings: Routine jimsteeg requests are inconsistent with the effective directive.
The sampled MATH-PROGRAMME merge launched twelve unrelated standalone CMDG push workflows and a 15 minute 56 second policy run.
Known-path classification and main-push path gating are reversible operating changes.
The proposal creates no proxy, merge, activation, ratification, certification, or promotion authority.
conditions: Measure workflow count, runner minutes, elapsed time, human requests, and false-full-fanout events before and after remediation.
Target zero routine jimsteeg requests, at most one Human Steward action, and at least 70 percent median reduction for unrelated merges.
Retain a one-change rollback to conservative fanout on false negative.
Review after thirty days or twenty protected merges, whichever comes first.
residual_uncertainty: Long-run classifier false-negative rate is not yet measured.
